lookback_source.quote: Check all nutritional approaches performed after admission/entry or reentry to the facility and within the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: Columns 2 and 3 use a 7-day look-back period (Column 2 = performed prior to admission/entry or reentry and within the last 7 days; Column 3 = performed after admission/entry or reentry and within the last 7 days). Column 1 uses a different window: the assessment period is days 1 through 3 of the SNF PPS Stay starting with A2400B. Column 4 uses the last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay ending on A2400C. Under the general convention, the ARD is the last day of the observation period and counting is ARD + 6 previous calendar days for a 7-day window (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-21).

coding_levels.label: Parenteral/IV feeding
coding_levels.definition: Introduction of a nutritive substance into the body by means other than the intestinal tract (e.g., subcutaneous, intravenous).

source.quote: PARENTERAL/IV FEEDING Introduction of a nutritive substance into the body by means other than the intestinal tract (e.g., subcutaneous, intravenous).

coding_levels.label: Feeding tube – nasogastric or abdominal (PEG)
coding_levels.definition: Presence of any type of tube that can deliver food/nutritional substances/fluids directly into the gastrointestinal system. Examples include, but are not limited to, nasogastric tubes, gastrostomy tubes, jejunostomy tubes, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) tubes.

source.quote: FEEDING TUBE Presence of any type of tube that can deliver food/ nutritional substances/ fluids directly into the gastrointestinal system.

coding_levels.label: Mechanically altered diet
coding_levels.definition: Require change in texture of food or liquids (e.g., pureed food, thickened liquids). A diet specifically prepared to alter the texture or consistency of food to facilitate oral intake.

coding_levels.label: Therapeutic diet
coding_levels.definition: A diet intervention prescribed by a physician or other authorized nonphysician practitioner that provides food or nutrients via oral, enteral, and parenteral routes as part of treatment of disease or clinical condition, to modify, eliminate, decrease, or increase identified micro- and macro-nutrients in the diet (Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 2020).

source.quote: THERAPEUTIC DIET A therapeutic diet is a diet intervention prescribed by a physician or other authorized nonphysician practitioner that provides food or nutrients via oral, enteral, and parenteral routes as part of treatment of disease or clinical condition

conflicts.topic: Coexisting observation windows for K0520 columns

positions.claim: Columns 2 and 3 use a 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Check all nutritional approaches performed after admission/entry or reentry to the facility and within the 7-day look-back period.

positions.claim: Column 1 uses days 1 through 3 of the SNF PPS Stay and Column 4 uses the last 3 days of the SNF PPS Stay.

source.quote: Assessment period is days 1 through 3 of the SNF PPS Stay starting with A2400B

conflicts.resolution: Not a contradiction: the document assigns different observation periods to different columns of the same item. lookback_days records the 7-day window used for Columns 2 and 3; the 3-day SNF PPS Stay windows for Columns 1 and 4 are recorded in lookback_notes.

conflicts.topic: Whether the K0520A look-back may extend into the preadmission period

positions.claim: Item pages direct that Column 2 captures approaches performed prior to admission/entry or reentry (i.e., preadmission), and K0520A includes nutrition/hydration received at the hospital as an outpatient or inpatient.

source.quote: K0520A includes any and all nutrition and hydration received by the nursing home resident during the observation period either at the nursing home, at the hospital as an outpatient or an inpatient, provided they were administered for nutrition or hydration.

positions.claim: General convention states the look-back period does not extend into the preadmission period unless item instructions state otherwise, naming Section K as an exception.

source.quote: With the exception of certain items (e.g., some items in Sections J, K and O), the look-back period does not extend into the preadmission period unless the item instructions state otherwise.

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: the general convention names Section K as an exception and defers to item instructions, so the K0520 Column 2 preadmission instructions govern.
